title: RELIEF: Relieving Memory Pressure In SoCs Via Data Movement-Aware Accelerator Scheduling
problem: Data movement latency is a critical performance bottleneck when using on-chip accelerators in emerging heterogeneous architectures with limited main memory bandwidth. Contemporary schedulers remain oblivious to available peer-to-peer DMA mechanisms between accelerators and employ deadline-driven policies that do not optimize for data locality and memory efficiency.
motivation: As accelerator latencies continue to reduce in emerging heterogeneous architectures, the lack of data communication focus in contemporary schedulers will increasingly worsen execution times and energy consumption.
method: RELIEF schedules tasks based on laxity—how much spare time each task has before its deadline becomes critical. Rather than strictly meeting every deadline, it strategically delays tasks slightly when doing so lets data flow directly from one accelerator to another, bypassing the main memory bottleneck. This reduces memory congestion while keeping the system fair and guaranteeing all deadlines are ultimately met.
key_novelty: The core idea is exploiting deadline laxity—the spare time before tasks must meet their deadlines—to route data directly between accelerators instead of through main memory, significantly reducing memory bottlenecks.
contributions: RELIEF scheduling policy integrating data movement awareness with least-laxity driven scheduling for accelerator-rich SoCs
Achieves 50% more data forwards compared to state-of-the-art policies
Reduces main memory traffic by up to 32% and energy consumption by up to 18%
Improves QoS with 14% more task deadlines met and 14% reduction in worst-case deadline violations

metrics.other: 32% main memory traffic reduction; 14% more deadlines met; 14% worst-case deadline violation reduction; 50% increase in data forwards
